newsitem.title: GERMANY: German soldiers to be dismissed for racist attack.
newsitem.headline: German soldiers to be dismissed for racist attack.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe has decided to dismiss soldiers accused of beating up three foreigners in western Germany in a racist attack last week, an army spokesman said on Sunday.

Police arrested nine men after masked soldiers in uniform and helmets went on the rampage last Monday and threatened an Italian with a knife and clubbed two Turks with baseball bats, shouting racist abuse.

Three of the men were later released as police said they were not suspected of taking part in the violence but six remained in custody. Prosecutors said they would probably go on trial in six to eight weeks' time.
The foreigners were treated in hospital for head injuries.
Some 800 people protested against racist attacks on Saturday in Detmold, where the attack took place.
Army spokesman Hartmut Bagger told German radio on Sunday that racism tended to be a problem only for young army recruits.

Bagger said such traits usually disappeared once troops completed a thorough political education. The army said last week the suspects had all just joined the army and most of them were from former communist east Germany.

The news magazine Focus said in a report released ahead of publication on Monday that police in the northwestern city of Bielefeld had detained the suspected ringleader of the gang after finding extreme right-wing propaganda in his flat.
Ruehe and Bagger condemned the attack "in the strongest terms" saying it jeopardised the reputation of the German army at home and abroad.
The attack came a day after Chancellor Helmut Kohl praised German soldiers for a spectacular operation in which they airlifted 120 German and other nationals out of Albania.
